svg.aria-label: Twelve measures, each drawn as the full spread of the 161 Massachusetts towns that run their own K-12 district, with Lunenburg marked. It is 158th of 161 on spending per pupil and 82nd on the average tax bill.
svg.text: Where Lunenburg sits, measure by measure
Each line is all 161 towns that run their own K–12 district, from lowest to highest. The blue mark is Lunenburg; the grey line is the middle town.
The measures are in different units and share no axis. What repeats is the SPREAD — so a position can be read against how far apart the towns actually are.
Spent above what the state says its schools need
actual spending as a multiple of the town’s foundation budget
Average tax bill on a single-family home
That bill as a share of income per head
all property, FY2026, over SY2025 pupils
Share of the tax base that is business
foundation budget less the required local contribution, FY2026
What the town must raise per child
required local contribution, FY2026 — a floor, not a ceiling
Share of children from low-income families
Rank counts from the highest value down: 1st has the most.
